doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Hearing Kind of Blue, Cannonball and Coltrane
summary: A seventh grade teacher played Kind of Blue; Blue describes its impact, Columbia Record Club albums and Cannonball's tone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well jumping ahead a little bit, apparently you heard “Kind of Blue” played for you by a seventh grade teacher and that was it. Did you— what made the biggest impression on you?

Oh, the biggest impression of that. It grabbed me, Monk. He turned the music on and I listened and what was there — well the first tune was “So What” on the record, was “So What.” And the introduction and the bass, the you know, the free bass line that was there © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
then into the melody and it just — Jimmy Cobb’s on the cymbal. And it was on man. And yeah. That’s what grabbed me. And there’s no other explanation.
When you heard Cannonball followed by Coltrane, were you at the point — this is seventh grade now — can you recall a preference or distinguishing one from the other?

I didn’t have a preference, however, my ear gravitated more to the tenor, the tenor sound. And actually yeah, yeah. I really got through it — no, no they were both — I was in junior high when I was listening to both of them. Because what I did was I had the opportunity to join the Columbia Record Club. You know, ten albums for 99 cents and then they send you a new one each month and then you take it or not. But records that I bought I got “Kind of Blue” I got one of them by Stan Getz “Dear Old Stockholm,” Cannonball Adderley and Coltrane, it was “Grand Central,” [scats] no that’s the bridge, but and then my high school, one of my high school music teachers gave me a copy of “Giant Steps,” the album. Yeah. But the distinction, the tenor sound, I gravitated more towards the tenor. I still loved the alto sound. Cannon had it. He spoke, the way he spoke was just amazing.
Yeah. I’m a huge fan as well. And he had that tone that sort of leapt off the record.

Yeah he did. His tone, his sound would lift you. You know it would lift you off — if you were standing it lifted you off your feet, if you were sitting it lifted you off your chair. It was just amazing. For me, I could hear heaven in that sound. Yeah. It’s amazing.
